# ops-log

`log/<date>.md` is the shared daily log. Several sessions append to it during the day, often within minutes of each other.

Rules:
- Entries are APPENDED, never rewritten. A whole-file write erases whatever another session added since you last read it.
- Use the helper: `python tools/log_append.py --text "## HH:MM · area · title\n- body"` (append mode, then verifies the old content is a byte-prefix of the new).
- An appending shell redirect (`>>`) is acceptable. A single `>` is not.

files.tools/log_append.py:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Append-only writer for the shared daily log.

    python tools/log_append.py --text "## 11:00 · area · title\n- body" [--date 2026-09-14]

Opens the log in append mode (existing bytes cannot be truncated), then re-reads and
verifies the previous content is a byte-prefix of the new content. A literal \\n in
--text becomes a newline."""
import argparse, os, sys

p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
p.add_argument("--text", required=True)
p.add_argument("--date", default="2026-09-14")
a = p.parse_args()
root = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
path = os.path.join(root, "log", a.date + ".md")
before = open(path, "rb").read() if os.path.exists(path) else b""
entry = a.text.replace("\\n", "\n").rstrip("\n")
lead = "" if (not before or before.endswith(b"\n")) else "\n"
with open(path, "a", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as fh:
    fh.write(lead + "\n" + entry + "\n")
after = open(path, "rb").read()
if not after.startswith(before):
    sys.exit("VERIFY FAILED: previous content is not a prefix of the new content")
print("appended %d bytes to %s (verified prefix)" % (len(after) - len(before), os.path.relpath(path, root)))
